title: Revolution: An evolutionary framework for rtl generation driven by large language models
venue: 31st Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference (ASP-DAC)

publication.venue: 31st Asia and South Pacific Design Automation Conference (ASP-DAC)

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-driven RTL generation and power-performance-area optimization
mechanism.populationDetail: A multi-candidate population is re-divided each generation into Fail and Success groups by correctness; both groups participate in pooled survivor selection and are then re-segregated.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate archive is described; top candidates by each PPA metric are preserved within generational survivor selection.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Fail and Success groups are correctness-stratified subpopulations rather than islands; offspring allocation is proportional to their current sizes, and their available operator menus differ.
mechanism.generationDetail: Fix, Simplify, Explore, Refactor, and Improve use one parent, while Fusion merges two successful parents; the menu mixes unary modification and multi-parent fusion.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Each individual stores natural-language Feedback alongside Thought and Code; parent Feedback is included in later evolutionary prompts.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Fail parents are selected randomly because their fitnesses are identical; Success parents use roulette-wheel selection proportional to fitness. Fusion draws two successful parents, while other strategies use one.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Correctness-stratified Fail/Success subpopulations receive proportional offspring allocation and have different available prompt operators; the current population taxonomy has no dedicated category for this state-dependent dual-population organization.

provenance.citationWarning: Already cited in the survey for adaptive prompt selection, verbalized feedback, PPA objectives, and parent selection. Treat Fail/Success groups as reclassified subpopulations, not islands. The three tested backbones are separate configurations; routing/collaboration is not described. Chapter 6 primary-signal placement remains none because that subsection covers preference-based evaluation, which this paper does not use.
